answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. Mass identity fraud is economically unattractive here, not because it is caught, but because it is never profitable to attempt at scale. Picture a island field, a echo in flight, a hollow in the distance — a natural triad mirroring how layered signals resist a single-point forgery.
